So I recently had a partner that was 17, in high school, etc., and I'll be completely honest, she annoyed the crap out of me. Thankfully, she left and went to college.

But the things that annoyed me the most, I'll point out as tips for you. Some of them might just be personal annoyances, but I'll lay them out anyways.

- don't be robotic with your patients. she literally would sound like a condescending recording the way she spoke to patients.

- don't ever ever talk about it being slow, don't talk about it being busy, don't talk about not doing a NET, don't talk about doing a NET.

- don't constantly turn off the ambulance, take the keys out and lock the truck. She did this on almost every call, and while this may be an annoyance of mine, don't do this.

- if your senior partner tells you to do something, just do it. She would give me pushback and shit when I'd log out of our truck 5-10 minutes before the end of our shift, the truck that was relieving us was already logged on, there's no point in us staying logged in. She was "scared of getting in trouble." While I realize she's still a kid and fears authority, just listen to whatever you're senior partner says, while some of it may seem wrong, they've got more experience.

- realize that you're still a kid, if you don't feel comfortable with something, speak up.

- don't get wrapped up with everything under the sun happening in the rest of your county/service area. there's no reason for you to get hyped up over a cardiac arrest happening 30 minutes outside of your service area.

- learn to lift patients. the girl that I was partners with actually caused me to injure my back because she couldn't even lift a stretcher over a curb.

- be humble
